case_title: Nanda Gopalan v. State of Kerala
weapon: A bat made of coconut leaf stem; a stone
evidence_type: Eyewitness/family and independent witnesses (PW 1 to PW 8); medical evidence (PW 10, Exhibit P5); documentary evidence
mitigating_circumstances: Compromise between the parties, who are close relatives
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.324 and 326; rigorous imprisonment of 2 years (s.324) and 3 years (s.326); Rs.30,000 payable to the injured as compensation
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed: conviction affirmed, sentence reduced. Application to compound s.324 and quash s.326 on compromise dismissed
neutral_facts: On a morning in May 1999, at about 7.30 a.m., the accused allegedly attacked the victim with a bat made of coconut leaf stem. The victim fell down after the blow. The accused then sat on the victim's chest and caused injuries with a stone. The victim became unconscious and was taken to a hospital, where he remained an indoor patient for 32 days. A casualty medical officer examined the victim at about 8.45 a.m. and recorded multiple injuries: a through-and-through lacerated wound at the left angle of the mouth exposing the upper gum, with upper teeth missing; a lacerated wound over the left eyebrow; an incised wound over the bridge of the nose; a torn right ear exposing cartilage; contusions over the right jaw and left upper jaw with swelling and bleeding lacerations. The first information report was recorded, and the investigation conducted, by a prosecution witness who then sent the accused for trial. The prosecution examined the victim, the victim's two sons, the victim's wife, and three independent witnesses, and produced medical evidence and documents.
physical_harm: Multiple facial and head injuries (lacerations, incised wound, torn ear, contusions) with loss of upper teeth; unconsciousness; 32 days as indoor patient
key_evidence_accepted: Concurrent findings of the courts below that the prosecution case was proved, including on the nature of the charge (weapon); medical evidence of PW 10 and Exhibit P5
witness_credibility: Not assessed in detail by the Supreme Court; it noted the trial court held the prosecution case proved and did not disturb that finding
trial_duration: offence: 14 May 1999; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 31 October 2014; Supreme Court: 24 April 2015
legal_representation: Appellant: Ram Jethmalani, senior counsel, appearing as amicus curiae (with others listed in the report); State of Kerala: Jogy Scaria
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation conducted; accused sent up for trial
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted and sentenced. High Court: conviction affirmed, sentence reduced; compounding application dismissed. Supreme Court: sentence reduced to period already undergone; compensation increased to Rs.2 lakhs
prosecution_argument: Convictions under ss.324 and 326 were rightly recorded and no interference was called for
defence_argument: Compromise should be considered to reduce sentence; weapon was not of the nature specified in ss.324/326, so charge could be altered to ss.323 and 325
legal_principle_applied: A plea that the weapon was not dangerous, not raised below and unsupported by evidence, cannot be raised for the first time in the Supreme Court; sentence to reflect proportionality between crime and punishment; compounding only as permitted under s.320 CrPC
precedent_relied_upon: Dasan v. State of Kerala (2014) 12 SCC 666; Mathai v. State of Kerala (2005) 3 SCC 260; Anwarul Haq v. State of U.P. (2005) 10 SCC 581; State of M.P. v. Ghanshyam Singh (2003) 8 SCC 13; Bankat v. State of Maharashtra (2005) 1 SCC 343
sentencing_rationale: Just and appropriate sentence keeping in mind proportion between crime and punishment and facts of the case; compromise between close relatives justified sentence reduction
judicial_mitigating_factors: Compromise between the parties, who are close relatives
other_sentence_order: Compensation increased to Rs.2 lakhs to be paid to the victim within three months, failing which the High Court sentence stands affirmed
